parameters.content:
## C - Publisher

Runs every 30 minutes (:13 and :43) or on demand.

**Scheduling is handed to Facebook.** A row more than 10 minutes out is
sent with `published=false` + `scheduled_publish_time`, and Facebook
publishes it at the slot, so n8n need not be awake at 10:00. A row
whose slot already arrived is published immediately, so nothing is
lost to downtime.

**Two ways to authenticate**, set by `AUTH_MODE` in config:

`oauth` - open the *Facebook OAuth (login)* credential, paste App ID and
Secret, click **Connect my account**; Facebook's own login window
opens. Needs a redirect URI whitelisted in the Meta app.

`token` - paste a long-lived **user** token into *Facebook User Token*.
No redirect URI needed; the Graph API Explorer issues one directly.

Either way the run derives the **Page** token itself via
`/me/accounts`, so nothing is copied twice and `FB_PAGE_ID` is
optional when the account manages one Page.

**DRY_RUN is ON by default.** Everything runs except the Facebook calls,
and the exact request bodies land in `errors_log`. Set `DRY_RUN=false`
in config when you are ready to post.

Status flow: `queued` -> `posting` (claimed) -> `scheduled` (accepted by
Facebook) or `posted` (published now) / `failed` / `skipped`.

### Double-post protection

`Claim Row` updates the row **only if its status is still what we read**
(both `id` and `status` must match). If another run got there first,
zero rows change, `Verify Claim` sees no updated row, and this run
stops without calling Facebook.

That is why the claim happens first, and why every HTTP node sits
behind it.

### Image fallback

The photo is uploaded by URL first. If Facebook cannot fetch it
(Pinterest hotlink protection), the bytes are downloaded in n8n and
uploaded as a file instead.

nodes.name: Every 30 Minutes
nodes.notes: Off :00/:30 deliberately - those are the busiest scheduler minutes.

nodes.name: Live Mode?
nodes.notes: TRUE = really posting, so a Page token is needed. A dry run skips the Facebook calls entirely and needs no credential.

nodes.name: OAuth Mode?
nodes.notes: AUTH_MODE in config. oauth = the login credential; token = a pasted long-lived user token. Both end at Pick Page.

nodes.name: FB List Pages (OAuth)
nodes.notes: Uses the Facebook login. Needs a redirect URI whitelisted in the Meta app.

nodes.name: FB List Pages (Token)
nodes.notes: Uses a pasted long-lived USER token. No redirect URI needed - the Graph API Explorer issues one directly.

nodes.name: Pick Page
nodes.notes: Chooses the Page (by FB_PAGE_ID, or the only one on the account) and keeps its token in memory for this execution only.

nodes.name: Log Auth Problem
nodes.notes: Login or Page resolution failed. The message says which, and what to do.

nodes.name: Boards Loaded
nodes.notes: Single-item gate - keeps the next table read from running N times.

nodes.name: Items Loaded
nodes.notes: Single-item gate - keeps the next table read from running N times.

nodes.name: Select To Publish
nodes.notes: All the selection rules. Unit-tested in src/publisher.test.js (24 cases).

nodes.name: Apply Skip
nodes.notes: A disabled board or broken data is recorded on the row itself, not just in the log.

nodes.name: Loop Publish
nodes.notes: One post at a time: each needs its own claim before any HTTP call.

nodes.name: Claim Row
nodes.notes: ATOMIC CLAIM. Matches on id AND current status, so a row already taken by another run updates zero rows.

nodes.name: Log Lost Race
nodes.notes: Another run owned the row. Not an error - this is the guard working.

nodes.name: Log Dry Run
nodes.notes: What WOULD have been sent to Facebook, including the exact URLs and the scheduled publish time.

nodes.name: Release Row
nodes.notes: Puts the row back exactly as it was - a dry run costs no attempt.

nodes.name: FB Upload Photo By URL
nodes.notes: Step 1 of 2. Facebook fetches the image itself.

nodes.name: Download Image

parameters.name: User-Agent

nodes.notes: Fallback: Facebook could not fetch the URL, so we fetch the bytes.

nodes.name: FB Upload Photo Binary
nodes.notes: Uploads the downloaded bytes as a file instead of a URL.

nodes.name: Media Id
nodes.notes: Reads the photo id from whichever upload path ran.

nodes.name: FB Create Post
nodes.notes: Step 2 of 2. published=false + scheduled_publish_time makes Facebook publish it at the slot.

nodes.name: Handle Result
nodes.notes: Maps the Graph response (or its error) onto the row update.

nodes.name: Write Publish Log
nodes.notes: The run report, including every failure with its Graph API error message.
